questions.q: Propanone and methanamine are treated with NaBH₃CN at pH 6–7. The product is:
questions.explain: A primary amine partner gives a secondary amine: the N-methyl imine is reduced to (CH₃)₂CH–NH–CH₃. NaBH₃CN at this pH reduces the iminium ion, not the ketone.

questions.q: Why can an aldehyde, an amine and NaBH₃CN be mixed in one pot for reductive amination?
options: NaBH₃CN is a stronger reductant than NaBH₄
At pH about 6–7 NaBH₃CN reduces the iminium ion much faster than the carbonyl compound
NaBH₃CN dehydrates the hemiaminal but does not reduce anything
questions.explain: Sodium cyanoborohydride is weaker than NaBH₄, so it leaves the aldehyde or ketone alone and selectively reduces the protonated imine.

questions.q: Cyclohexanone oxime is treated separately with (P) Na/C₂H₅OH and (Q) acid. The products of P and Q respectively are:
questions.explain: Reduction cleaves the N–O bond and saturates C=N to give the primary amine, while an oxime in acid undergoes the Beckmann rearrangement to an amide.

questions.q: Which amine CANNOT be obtained by reductive amination of a carbonyl compound using NH₃ and H₂/Ni as the only reagents?
questions.explain: NH₃ gives a primary amine; a secondary amine such as N-methylethanamine needs a primary amine (CH₃NH₂) as the nitrogen partner.
